observable_features: Reports the separately defined function value when asked for a two-sided limit at a removable discontinuity.
Treats a filled point as overriding matching left- and right-hand behavior.
evidence_required: Compare the learner's stated limit with the approach values and the function value in one representation.
Ask the learner to distinguish what x approaches from what happens exactly at the point.
alternative_causes: The learner may have misread the requested x-value rather than confused limit and function value.
The learner may have made an arithmetic error after correctly identifying the approaching value.
misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Contrast nearby behavior with the value at the point, then require the learner to name each quantity before calculating.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and explicitly distinguish the limit from the function value.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Request one explanation that separately states the nearby behavior and the value at the point.

observable_features: Checks only that the function value exists, or only that the limit exists, when deciding continuity at a point.
Chooses a parameter without equating the two-sided limit and the defined function value.
evidence_required: Require the learner to state all three point-continuity conditions and apply each at the named point.
Use a piecewise example in which the limit and the function value can be varied independently.
alternative_causes: The learner may know the conditions but omit them because the prompt was read as computation only.
The learner may correctly set up continuity but make an equation-solving error.

prerequisite_rationale.u1-limit-value-substitution: Continuity at a point requires treating the limiting value and the defined value as distinct quantities before comparing them.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Have the learner label existence of the value, existence of the two-sided limit, and equality of those quantities before solving.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and cite the required continuity or IVT conditions.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for the three continuity conditions on a fresh piecewise function without asking for any parameter calculation.

observable_features: Reports a function value or a raw output change when the derivative at a point is requested.
Interprets derivative notation without a per-unit-input rate or tangent-slope meaning.
evidence_required: Ask for a difference quotient from nearby values and a sentence interpreting its units or slope.
Compare the learner's derivative estimate with the scale of both the output change and the input change.
alternative_causes: The learner may calculate the quotient correctly but copy the wrong table entry.
The learner may understand the rate but omit units in a context-free response.

prerequisite_rationale.u1-limit-value-substitution: The derivative definition depends on separating a limiting process from the function value at the evaluation point.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Rebuild the derivative as output change divided by input change, then connect that quotient to the local tangent slope.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and interpret the derivative with sign and units.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for one nearby secant-slope estimate and a one-sentence interpretation before assigning a conceptual cause.

observable_features: Differentiates a product as the product of the two derivatives.
Includes only one of the two product-rule terms or loses a factor from one term.
evidence_required: Ask the learner to differentiate a product whose expanded derivative can be checked independently.
Require labeling of the unchanged factor in each of the two product-rule terms.
alternative_causes: The learner may know the product rule but make a derivative error in one factor.
The learner may mistake multiplication notation for function composition.

prerequisite_rationale.u2-derivative-not-rate: Product-rule work presupposes that each factor's derivative is a local rate rather than another function value.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Use a two-column product-rule structure showing which factor changes in each term, then verify by expansion when possible.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and preserve both product-rule contributions.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for the derivative of one simple polynomial product both by expansion and by the product rule.

observable_features: Differentiates the outer function but omits the derivative of the inner function.
Multiplies by the inner function itself instead of by its derivative.
evidence_required: Ask the learner to name the inner and outer functions before differentiating a composition.
Check the proposed derivative at one numerical input against a finite local change or an independently expanded form.
alternative_causes: The learner may know the chain rule but make an algebraic simplification error.
The expression may have been read as a product rather than a composition.

prerequisite_rationale.u2-derivative-not-rate: The chain rule combines local rates, so interpreting each derivative as a rate is a conceptual prerequisite.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Require an inner-outer decomposition and leave a visible factor for the inner derivative before any simplification.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and include the correct inner-rate factor.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask the learner to identify only the inner function and its derivative for a new composition.

observable_features: Differentiates a term containing y with respect to x but omits the dy/dx factor.
Treats y as a constant throughout an implicit relation.
evidence_required: Ask the learner to annotate which quantities depend on x before differentiating.
Use an implicit equation with a known point and compare the resulting slope with local geometric behavior.
alternative_causes: The learner may include dy/dx correctly and then solve the linear equation for it incorrectly.
The learner may substitute the point before differentiating and erase variable dependence.

prerequisite_rationale.u3-chain-rule-inner-factor: Differentiating a function of y with respect to x is a chain-rule application whose inner rate is dy/dx.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Mark every y-term as a composition with y(x), differentiate one term at a time, and collect all dy/dx terms.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and retain every required dy/dx factor.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask the learner to differentiate only y squared and xy with respect to x, without solving a full equation.

observable_features: Interprets a derivative as an amount rather than a rate and omits per-input units.
Ignores the derivative's sign when describing contextual change.
evidence_required: Require a sentence containing the evaluation time, direction of change, magnitude, and quotient units.
Compare the learner's interpretation with the units assigned to both variables.
alternative_causes: The learner may understand the rate but omit units from a terse numerical answer.
A negative sign may be lost through arithmetic rather than interpretation.

prerequisite_rationale.u2-derivative-not-rate: Contextual interpretation requires the derivative's prior meaning as a signed output change per unit input.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Use a four-part interpretation frame: at what input, which quantity, increasing or decreasing, and at what rate with units.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and communicate sign, magnitude, and quotient units.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for the numerator and denominator units of one derivative before requesting a full contextual sentence.

observable_features: Substitutes snapshot values before differentiating and thereby treats changing quantities as constants.
Relates the variables correctly but omits one time-derivative factor after implicit differentiation.
evidence_required: Ask for the relation in variables and its time derivative before any numerical substitution.
Check the final rate's sign and units against the stated motion or growth.
alternative_causes: The learner may differentiate correctly but use a wrong geometric formula.
The learner may make an arithmetic error after a complete related-rates setup.

prerequisite_rationale.u3-implicit-y-prime-omission: Related-rates equations require implicit differentiation of quantities that depend on time.
prerequisite_rationale.u4-context-derivative-units: The requested related rate must be interpreted with a direction and quotient units.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Separate the work into relation, differentiation with respect to time, snapshot substitution, solution, and contextual unit check.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 using variable-first differentiation and valid units.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Request only the undifferentiated relation and its time derivative for a fresh geometry context.

observable_features: Tests only where the derivative is zero and omits endpoints or in-domain nondifferentiable points.
Labels every critical point as an absolute extremum without comparing candidate values.
evidence_required: Require a complete candidate list and the function value at every candidate on a closed interval.
Ask the learner to distinguish critical points, local extrema, and absolute extrema.
alternative_causes: The learner may know the candidate process but solve the derivative equation incompletely.
The learner may omit an endpoint because the interval was copied incorrectly.

prerequisite_rationale.u2-derivative-not-rate: Identifying critical points requires knowing where the derivative is zero or fails to exist in the function's domain.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Build a candidate table containing both endpoints and all in-domain critical points, then compare actual function values.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and justify extrema from a complete candidate set.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask the learner to list candidates only, without yet choosing extrema, for one new closed-interval function.

observable_features: Uses the sign of the first derivative rather than whether the first derivative is increasing or decreasing to determine concavity.
Names an inflection point where the second derivative is zero but its sign does not change.
evidence_required: Ask whether the slope values are increasing or decreasing on each interval and connect that behavior to concavity.
Require a sign-change check around every proposed inflection input.
alternative_causes: The learner may understand concavity but differentiate the first derivative incorrectly.
The learner may confuse an interval statement with the coordinates of an inflection point.

prerequisite_rationale.u2-product-rule-distribution: Accurate second-derivative analysis depends on reliably differentiating first-derivative expressions that may include products.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Translate between increasing or decreasing slopes and the sign of the second derivative before locating sign changes.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and justify concavity and inflection by sign change.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask whether a short table of first-derivative values is increasing or decreasing before using concavity vocabulary.

observable_features: Adds all geometric areas as positive when a signed accumulation or net change is requested.
Reports signed accumulation when the prompt instead asks for total accumulated magnitude.
evidence_required: Require separate labels for signed contribution and geometric area on intervals above and below the axis.
Ask for both net change and total magnitude from the same simple rate graph.
alternative_causes: The learner may distinguish signed and total accumulation but calculate one region's area incorrectly.
The learner may misread which quantity the prompt requests.
misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Partition at sign changes, record each interval's signed contribution, and only then decide whether absolute values are needed.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and distinguish signed accumulation from total magnitude.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for the sign of each region on one fresh rate graph before requesting any sum.

observable_features: Evaluates the integrand at a variable bound but omits the derivative of that bound.
Applies the upper-bound contribution with the wrong sign when both integration limits vary.
evidence_required: Ask the learner to label upper and lower bound contributions before differentiating.
Check the proposed derivative at a numerical input using maintained table values for the integrand.
alternative_causes: The learner may apply the FTC correctly but substitute a table value from the wrong input.
The learner may make a sign error while distributing a negative lower-bound term.

prerequisite_rationale.u3-chain-rule-inner-factor: A variable integration limit is an inner function whose derivative multiplies the integrand value.
prerequisite_rationale.u6-signed-accumulation-area: The sign of each moving-bound contribution follows the orientation of signed accumulation.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Write one signed term for each moving bound and leave each bound derivative visible until after substitution.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 including every bound derivative and orientation sign.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for only the upper-bound and lower-bound terms of a new accumulation derivative before simplification.

observable_features: Reads a slope-field segment's vertical coordinate as the derivative value.
Infers a solution's behavior from one segment while ignoring how slopes change across the field.
evidence_required: Ask for the slope represented by segments at several labeled coordinates.
Require a qualitative solution path that remains tangent to nearby field segments.
alternative_causes: The learner may understand segment meaning but misread a coordinate label.
The learner may reverse positive and negative visual slopes.

prerequisite_rationale.u4-context-derivative-units: A slope-field segment represents the signed local rate dy/dx at a location, extending contextual derivative interpretation.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: At each marked point, separate the point's y-coordinate from the small segment's rise-over-run before tracing a solution.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and justify behavior from local segment slopes.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask for the slopes of three explicitly described field segments without asking for a full solution curve.

observable_features: Finds a family of antiderivatives but does not use the initial condition to determine its constant.
Drops an absolute-value or branch condition during separation and accepts a solution outside its stated domain.
evidence_required: Require both the general separated solution and a visible substitution of the initial condition.
Substitute the proposed particular solution into the differential equation and initial condition.
alternative_causes: The learner may use the initial condition correctly but solve the resulting constant equation incorrectly.
The learner may produce an equivalent constant form that only appears different.

prerequisite_rationale.u6-ftc-variable-bound-chain: Constructing and checking a particular solution relies on linking derivatives and antiderivatives with correct variable dependence.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Keep an explicit arbitrary constant through integration, apply the initial condition, and verify both the equation and initial value.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and verify the differential equation and initial condition.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask the learner to substitute one proposed family into only the initial condition and solve for its constant.

observable_features: Uses the signed integral of velocity as total distance even when velocity changes sign.
Uses absolute velocity for displacement or net position change.
evidence_required: Require the learner to locate velocity sign changes and compute both displacement and total distance.
Compare the integral result with position values at endpoints and turning times.
alternative_causes: The learner may understand the distinction but miss a zero of velocity.
The learner may calculate one geometric area incorrectly after partitioning correctly.

prerequisite_rationale.u6-signed-accumulation-area: Distance and displacement specialize the distinction between total magnitude and signed accumulation.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Partition at velocity zeros, record signed changes in position, and use absolute contributions only for total distance.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 and distinguish displacement from total distance.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask the learner to identify the velocity sign intervals before requesting either accumulated quantity.

observable_features: Uses function values as radii without measuring distance from the stated axis of rotation.
Reverses outer and inner radii or omits the squared-radius difference for a washer.
evidence_required: Require labeled inner and outer radius expressions as distances from the axis before writing an integral.
Check that each radius is nonnegative and that the outer radius is at least the inner radius throughout the interval.
alternative_causes: The learner may identify both radii correctly but expand or integrate the polynomial incorrectly.
The learner may choose the wrong integration variable after reading the region description.

prerequisite_rationale.u6-signed-accumulation-area: Washer volume accumulates nonnegative cross-sectional area and requires maintaining the orientation of a definite integral.

misconceptions.minimum_remediation: Draw or describe one representative washer, measure both radii from the rotation axis, and verify outer exceeds inner.
misconceptions.exit_standard: Correctly complete the unseen transfer item independently with hint level 0 using valid outer and inner radius distances.
misconceptions.uncertain_action: Ask only for the two radius expressions at a generic slice before requesting a volume integral.
